title: Which monodromy groups do Jacobian counterexamples have?
W: A Keller map (polynomial map with constant nonzero Jacobian) that is not invertible covers a generic point d times, and following the d preimages around loops gives a permutation group, its monodromy. Campbell's 1973 theorem says that if this group is regular (the Galois case), the map is invertible. The 2026 counterexamples realize full symmetric groups and some imprimitive groups. Is Campbell's theorem the only obstruction?
M: For a Keller map $F:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C^n$ ($\det JF\in\mathbb C^\times$) of geometric degree $d$, let $\mathrm{Mon}(F)\le S_d$ be the monodromy group of a general fibre, i.e. the Galois group of the Galois closure of $\mathbb C(x)/\mathbb C(F)$ acting on the $d$ embeddings. It is transitive, and by Campbell's theorem it is regular only when $F$ is an automorphism ($d=1$). Determine the set $\mathcal M$ of transitive permutation groups (up to permutation isomorphism) arising as $\mathrm{Mon}(F)$ for non-invertible Keller maps in some dimension (stabilization $F\times\mathrm{id}$ preserves $\mathrm{Mon}$). Is $\mathcal M$ exactly the set of non-regular transitive groups? Test case: is the alternating group $A_d$ ($d\ge4$, natural action) in $\mathcal M$? Is every member of $\mathcal M$ realized already in dimension $3$?
why: Since the Jacobian conjecture was refuted in 2026, the field has produced dozens of explicit counterexamples, and monodromy is the invariant used to tell them apart (S_3 for Alpöge's map, S_N for weighted lifts, the imprimitive groups G_n of marked-root maps of order m^n n!/gcd(2,m)). The geometric degree question is settled: every d >= 3 occurs. Monodromy is the next coarse invariant, and it is not settled. The only general constraint is Campbell's Galois theorem, together with older two-dimensional Galois-theoretic results (Razar, Wright). An inverse-Galois-type classification would say exactly how much of the classical Galois approach to the conjecture was ever viable. A new obstruction (for example, that alternating groups never occur) would be a structural theorem about étale maps of affine space.
diagnosis: 'Classify all non-invertible Keller maps of C^3' is vague and hopeless: infinitely many families are already known, with no workable notion of complete list. Importance was high; well-posedness and attackability were missing.
what_changed: Replaced the classification by the coarse invariant that the literature actually uses, the monodromy group. Asked the inverse problem: is Campbell the only obstruction? Gave a decisive test case (A_d) and a dimension-3 refinement. Geometric degree was rejected because it is already settled.

title: Critical Ising on the hat is SLE(3)
W: Show the interface in the critical Ising model on a hat tiling converges to the random curve SLE(3), even though the graph is not isoradial.
M: For the critical Ising model on the hat graph with Dobrushin boundary conditions, prove the interface converges to chordal SLE$_3$.
why: Original reviewer note: scorer note: Ising universality beyond isoradial graphs; hat is a good test case.
diagnosis: One test case (the hat, uniform couplings) of the broad open problem of Ising universality on aperiodic, non-isoradial planar graphs. The sibling N-344 is already STAYS_B for the same reason.
what_changed: Nothing. Current s-embedding theory (Chelkak; 2512.10142, 2512.20361) gives conformal invariance whenever a suitable s-embedding exists, so the general version reduces to known broad open problems. The canonical upgrade is famous-adjacent, not novel.

title: Explicit Navier–Stokes blow-up
W: Write down a forced Navier–Stokes blow-up as an explicit formula instead of a computer-assisted construction.
M: Give closed-form smooth $u_0,f$ on $\mathbb{R}^3$ for which the Navier–Stokes solution blows up in finite time.
why: Original reviewer note: scorer note: Explicit formula for known computer-assisted blow-up; meaningful but derivative.
diagnosis: 'Closed form' is not a mathematical property, so the problem is ill-posed. It is also derivative. Its premise looks false: the 2026 forced blow-up is described as an analytical proof with Lean formalization, not as computer-assisted.
what_changed: Dropped. No precise version keeps the novelty. The structural siblings (steady force, N-360; unforced blow-up) are Millennium-level.

title: Finite simple groups in Lean
W: Turn the classification of finite simple groups into one computer-checked proof.
M: Formalize the classification of finite simple groups in Lean 4.
why: Original reviewer note: scorer note: CFSG formalization: major engineering, not a math question per se.
diagnosis: An engineering and formalization project, not an open mathematical question. Formalizing CFSG is a widely discussed long-term goal, so it is not novel as a 'problem'.
what_changed: Dropped. It has no mathematical yes/no content to sharpen.

title: Word equations with square-free unknowns
W: Solving equations between words with unknown pieces is decidable (Makanin), even with regular constraints on the unknowns. What if some unknowns must be square-free, meaning they contain no block repeated twice in a row? Square-freeness is not a regular property.
M: Let $A=\{a,b,c\}$ and let $\mathrm{SF}\subseteq A^*$ be the set of square-free words. Is the existential first-order theory of $(A^*,\cdot,a,b,c,\mathrm{SF})$ decidable? Equivalently: given a finite system of word equations with constants together with constraints $x_i\in\mathrm{SF}$ or $x_i\notin\mathrm{SF}$, can one decide whether it has a solution?
diagnosis: A clean, apparently unposed question, but niche. Negative constraints are trivial: x not in SF is existentially definable (x = p w w s, w nonempty). Only positive SF constraints matter, and over a binary alphabet SF is finite. The ternary positive case remains.
what_changed: Nothing. Equivalent form: does a word-equation EDT0L solution language (Ciobanu-Diekert-Elder) meet SF in given coordinates? The general version (pattern-avoidance constraints) is broader but no more important; the length-constraint problem dominates the field.

title: Burgers with degenerate critical dissipation
W: Critical half-Laplacian dissipation keeps Burgers smooth. Let that dissipation switch off quadratically at one point of the circle. Do shocks form there?
M: Let $a(x)=1-\cos x$ and consider $u_t+uu_x+\Lambda^{1/2}\big(a\,\Lambda^{1/2}u\big)=0$ on $\mathbb{T}$, $\Lambda=(-\partial_x^2)^{1/2}$. Decide whether every real $u_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb{T})$ yields a global smooth solution.
why: Original reviewer note: deep vet grade C: Likely routine, with expected answer no. The equation preserves odd symmetry (a is even), so odd data with u_0'(0)<0 steepen at the stationary point x=0. diagnosis: Graded C. Odd symmetry pins steepening at the zero of a. Scaling shows that degeneracy of order beta > 1/3 makes the dissipation subcritical at the Burgers shock scale, so stable shock formation applies routinely. Answer: no.
what_changed: Nothing. The best variant is the sharp threshold for a ~ |x|^beta: blow-up iff beta > 1/3 (heuristic). It is still narrow, the regime beta < 1/3 is likely a modulus-of-continuity exercise, and the importance does not rise to A.

title: Thue–Morse Lorenz knots
W: Turn the first 2^n letters of the Thue–Morse word into a periodic orbit of the Lorenz flow, and so into a knot K_n. For n >= 4 these knots appear to be hyperbolic. Their volume grows only in proportion to n, the logarithm of the word length, not in proportion to the length itself. Prove that, and find the constant.
M: Let $K_n$ be the Lorenz knot with Lorenz word $t_0t_1\cdots t_{2^n-1}$ (the length-$2^n$ Thue–Morse prefix, $0\mapsto x$, $1\mapsto y$; this word is primitive, since Thue–Morse is overlap-free and $t_{[0,2^n)}=w\bar w$). Prove that $S^3\setminus K_n$ is hyperbolic for all $n\ge4$ and that $\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathrm{vol}(S^3\setminus K_n)/n$ exists and is positive. Determine the limit.
why: Original reviewer note: deep vet grade C: The ORIGINAL claim (vol/2^n tends to a positive limit) appears FALSE. I computed K_n as the closure of the Lorenz permutation braid of the sorted cyclic shifts and used SnapPy. n=2 gives the unknot and n=3 gives the torus knot T(3,4), with fundamental group <a,b | a^4=b^3>. For n=4
diagnosis: Graded C. The family is arbitrary (Thue-Morse prefixes). The original vol/2^n claim was numerically false and was rewritten to vol ~ c n. An O(n) upper bound likely follows routinely from twist-region volume bounds for T-links; the limit is narrow.
what_changed: Nothing. The structural version, 'Lorenz knots of substitution words have volume linear in the substitution level' (Sturmian/Christoffel words give torus knots), is natural-ish but niche, and it is unverified beyond n = 8. No literature check found it posed.
